perf_validation.approach: Flavor A + distance-dedup (Dalton-directed after the 1200-cap re-measure): 3s decimation + groupArray-per-(kit,hour) + arraySort + arrayFold distance-dedup (drop points <~5m/16ft from the last KEPT point; collapses idle-scanner dwell, keeps moving routes full-fidelity) + 1200 hard-ceiling cap; HistoricPathBuilder in PHP over the bounded result.
perf_validation.measurement: Read-only prod CH (Cloud, clarity DB, v26.2). Worst-case multi-kit window = 40 busiest kit_mappings over 7d (incl. a 2.23M-row/7d always-on idle scanner). Query SHAPE: 3s-decimation inner (argMin coords per toStartOfInterval(timestamp_utc, INTERVAL 3 SECOND), lower(kit_mapping) IN(?) + timestamp_utc range) -> outer GROUP BY (mapping, toStartOfHour(ts)) materializing arraySlice(arraySort(x->x.1, groupArray(tuple(ts,lng,lat))), 1, 200). AGGREGATES: 6.40M raw rows / 1.58M decimated points collapse to 2,401 grouped (kit,hour) rows to PHP; server-side 200-cap bounds payload to 452,622 coords (~11.7MB JSON); CH query 462ms. All SQL functions execute on prod CH. Consistent with Dalton's org-14 All-Kits/30d guidance numbers (~4,066 rows / ~750k coords / ~90MB). BUILD NOTE: cap MUST be applied IN the SELECT (materialize only the capped sorted array) so only bounded coords cross the wire/into PHP. No raw rows recorded.
perf_validation.php_memory_measurement: Measured the ACTUAL controller assembly path (flat points -> HistoricPathBuilder::build -> rows -> json_encode) in tinker: 100,000 points => 143.9 MB peak (~1,509 bytes/point); 300,000 points OOM'd the process. PHP memory_limit here = 256M (repo sets no web limit; prod FrankenPHP unknown). So the safe ceiling ~= 140K points (200MB). Extrapolated: org-14 All-Kits/30d (2.3M points) ~= 3.3 GB -> hard OOM (heavier than the guidance's ~300MB because the real end-to-end PHP path uses assoc arrays + intermediate copies, ~1.5KB/point). NORMAL use is safe: single kit/shift ~3K pts ~5MB; single kit/7d ~21K ~32MB; single kit/30d ~90K ~135MB. Danger is only multi-kit x long-range. Cause = sc_positions (continuous, 5-10x the old scan-only kit_scan_paths point count; the old sparse source never OOM'd — that sparseness was the bug). Dalton-approved fix: replace the kit-days guard with a memory-safe pre-flight point-count guard (MAX_RENDER_POINTS ~120K ~= 180MB, under 256M) that refuses over-budget selections BEFORE the heavy data enters PHP; dedup + 1200 cap retained. Will re-confirm empirically in agent QA (drive a large selection, watch peak memory).
perf_validation.approach_swap_note: Re-measured the dedup'd shipped query at prod scale (40 busiest mappings/30d, same heavy proxy): 9,915 kit-hour rows, 6,114,184 coords (vs 7,024,657 pre-dedup — only 13% reduction), ~525MB PHP est, CH query 5,868ms. WHY ONLY 13%: the busiest mappings are MOVING-heavy, not dwell-heavy; dedup correctly collapses stationary dwell (verified: 100 stationary+10 moving -> 11; slow crawl 30@3m -> 15) but has little to remove on genuine movement. Realistic largest REAL org (org-14 ~39 kits, per Dalton's guidance) All-Kits/30d ~= 2.3M coords ~= ~300MB (the 'no-cap' number Dalton already measured/accepted), survivable, and dedup helps more there if org-14 has idle kits. The moving-heavy pessimistic proxy (~525MB/6s) is NOT a real single org and is bounded by MAX_KIT_DAYS=2000. dedup is a correctness win (no redundant dwell) + helps idle-heavy orgs, but is NOT a magic bound for busy fleets. Further levers = lossy coarsening or a tighter guard. SURFACED TO DALTON for proceed-vs-tighten decision.
perf_validation.remeasure_1200_cap: After RN1 forced the cap 200->1200 (to fix the continuity truncation), re-measured the SHIPPED 1200-cap read-only on prod CH: 40 busiest mappings / 30d = 9,822 kit-hour rows, 7,024,657 coords (vs 1,852,419 at cap=200), ~600MB PHP est, CH query 9,122ms. Scales to ~1GB / ~15s near the MAX_KIT_DAYS=2000 guard boundary. The 1200-cap effectively removes the memory bound for heavy/idle-scanner-heavy selections (idle scanners tick ~1200 near-identical stationary pts/hour). Normal selections unaffected. SURFACED TO DALTON: the Option-1 (1200-cap + breadth guard) bound is weaker than the estimate the decision was based on; recommend distance-based dedup (collapse stationary points) as the reconciling fix. Awaiting decision before QA.

findings_residual: [NON-SCORING/accepted] lower(kit_mapping) defeats the PK on the sc_positions scan (inherited verbatim from OrgLivePathsQuery/KitHistoricPositionsQuery idiom; not a new regression).

[NON-SCORING/by-design] countPoints() is uncached (a cached count could go stale as data grows and slip an over-budget selection past the guard); so every request re-runs the CH assembly to sum lengths even on a data-cache hit. Correct-by-design per RN3 fresh lane; follow-up only if map refresh frequency is high at prod scale.

[NON-SCORING/accepted tradeoff] a genuinely-driving (non-idle) All-Kits/30d selection won't compress under dedup and will hit the 120K guard -> 422 (Dalton-directed: refuse rather than OOM). Real use (single kit / small group over a shift/week) is well under budget.

[NON-SCORING/tuning] budget headroom ~200MB total under the 256M limit is defensible but 'thinner than comfortable' for an all-moving fleet deduping near the cap; MAX_RENDER_POINTS could be lowered to ~100K if agent-QA's large-selection memory measurement shows it's tight.
